source_metadata.title: The Role of Diagnostics-Driven Antifungal Stewardship in the Management of Invasive Fungal Infections: A Systematic Literature Review

atoms.canonical_statement: The systematic literature review evaluated the role of diagnostics in antifungal stewardship programs and their impact on management of invasive fungal infections.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: evaluated the role of diagnostics in AFS programs

atoms.canonical_statement: PubMed and EMBASE were systematically searched for studies using both an antifungal stewardship approach and a diagnostic approach from January 2010 through January 2021, with manual reference-list searching also performed.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Systematic searches of PubMed and EMBASE were performed

atoms.canonical_statement: Eligible studies involved an antifungal stewardship program, evaluated patients with an invasive fungal infection indication, included a diagnostic approach, and reported at least two prespecified outcomes of interest.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: studies had ≥2 defined outcomes of interest

population.label: Studies considered for inclusion in the systematic review
inclusion_criteria: AFS program independent or part of AMS
At least two outcomes of interest reported

atoms.canonical_statement: Review articles, conference abstracts, and non-English-language articles were excluded.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Review articles, conference abstracts, and non-English-language articles were excluded.

population.label: Studies considered for inclusion in the systematic review

atoms.canonical_statement: Two researchers independently screened titles and abstracts, full texts were reviewed for shortlisted studies, and disagreements about inclusion were resolved with a third researcher.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: screening done independently by 2 researchers

atoms.canonical_statement: Extracted data included study characteristics, organism or condition, diagnostic approach, turnaround time, time to targeted therapy, antifungal consumption and cost, de-escalation or discontinuation, length of therapy, mortality, length of stay, and selected additional outcomes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Data from the eligible studies were extracted

atoms.canonical_statement: The review followed PRISMA methodology and used narrative qualitative synthesis without statistical methods.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: no statistical methods were used

atoms.canonical_statement: The review screened 422 citations, assessed 63 full-text articles, and included 17 articles that fulfilled all eligibility criteria.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: 17 articles that fulfilled all eligibility criteria were included

population.label: Studies included in the systematic review

atoms.canonical_statement: Among the 17 included studies, 8 were from Europe, 4 from the United States, 4 from Japan, and 1 from Thailand; most were single-center studies.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Europe (n = 8) and the United States (n = 4)

population.label: Studies included in the systematic review

atoms.canonical_statement: Eleven of 17 included studies evaluated Candida-related indications only, while 6 included one or more indications involving other fungal pathogens without species-stratified outcomes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: 11 studies were based only on Candida-related indications

population.label: Studies included in the systematic review

atoms.canonical_statement: Eleven included studies used pre- and postintervention methods to evaluate antifungal stewardship programs.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: 11 studies utilized pre- and postintervention methods

atoms.canonical_statement: Routine diagnostic methods were used in 9 of 17 studies; additional approaches included BDG testing in 7, galactomannan testing in 3, CT in 3, T2Candida in 2, MALDI-TOF in 2, PCR in 1, and PNA-FISH in 1.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: other diagnostic tools used were BDG test

atoms.canonical_statement: The abstract reported galactomannan testing in 4 of 17 included studies, whereas the Results section reported 3 of 17.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: galactomannan test (4/17)

atoms.canonical_statement: Diagnostics-driven antifungal stewardship interventions combined diagnostic testing or diagnostic recommendations with stewardship activities intended to optimize antifungal prescribing and management.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: utilized both an AFS and a diagnostic approach

exposures.details: AFS plus diagnostic testing or diagnostic recommendations

atoms.canonical_statement: Performance outcomes of interest included turnaround time, time to targeted therapy, antifungal consumption, antifungal cost savings, de-escalation or discontinuation, and length of therapy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: performance measures

outcome.definition: Turnaround time, time to targeted therapy, consumption, cost, de-escalation/discontinuation, and length of therapy

atoms.canonical_statement: Clinical outcomes of interest included mortality and hospital length of stay, with additional outcomes including clinical failure, adverse events, hospital-acquired candidemia, and Candida species prevalence.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: clinical measures (including mortality and LOS)

outcome.definition: Mortality, LOS, clinical failure, adverse events, hospital-acquired candidemia, and Candida species prevalence

atoms.canonical_statement: Heil et al. reported that PNA-FISH reduced median time to Candida species identification from 4 days with routine methods to 0.2 days.

atoms.canonical_statement: The review linked long turnaround times from batch testing and outsourced reference-laboratory testing with reduced ability to realize time-saving benefits of fungal diagnostics.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: batch testing ... lead to delayed TAT

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that diagnostics-driven antifungal stewardship can potentially improve antifungal consumption, cost, mortality, and length of stay without reported negative effects on patient outcomes.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: did not demonstrate any negative impact on patient outcomes

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors recommended fostering diagnostic tests that can yield results 24 hours every day to support timely and appropriate antifungal therapy.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: diagnostic tests yielding results 24 hours every day should be fostered

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors recommended that antifungal stewardship programs assess clinical indicators of patient outcomes in addition to cost savings from reduced antifungal consumption.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: must focus on clinical indicators

atoms.canonical_statement: The review identified limited implementation and reporting of antifungal stewardship in developing countries and highlighted access to advanced diagnostic techniques as a major challenge.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: gap in implementing and reporting AFS in developing countries

atoms.canonical_statement: Evidence available to evaluate diagnostics-driven antifungal stewardship interventions was limited, with few pre/post intervention studies.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Limited evidence was available to evaluate diagnostic-driven AFS interventions

atoms.canonical_statement: Heterogeneity in stewardship initiatives, study methods, and outcomes prevented direct comparison across studies.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: direct comparison across studies was not possible

atoms.canonical_statement: Most included studies were single-center studies with small patient numbers, limiting generalizability.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Most studies were conducted at single centers with small patient numbers

atoms.canonical_statement: Because most studies focused on Candida, evidence on diagnostic setup and challenges for other fungal pathogens was limited.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: most of the studies focused on Candida diagnosis

atoms.canonical_statement: Studies including more than one indication or pathogen generally did not stratify outcomes by species, preventing species-specific analysis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: separate analysis of outcomes based on species was not feasible

atoms.canonical_statement: Without appropriate control groups, the review could not fully separate benefits attributable to diagnostic testing plus stewardship from benefits of diagnostic testing alone.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: difficult to fully ascertain whether the benefits

atoms.canonical_statement: The review did not use statistical synthesis, so definitive conclusions require caution.

extraction_limitations: The governing LiteratureAtom workflow is designed for primary literature, while this source is a systematic literature review; atoms therefore represent claims reported by the review rather than re-extraction from each underlying primary study.
Study-level outcomes reproduced in the review were anchored to the review text/tables and were not independently verified against the cited original studies.

The source contains internal numeric inconsistencies, including galactomannan use reported as 4/17 studies in the abstract versus 3/17 in the Results, and mortality improvement described as 12 studies in the Mortality subsection versus 13 studies in the abstract/Discussion.
Whitney et al. turnaround-time labels appear internally inconsistent between narrative Results and Table 2; this was preserved and tagged rather than silently reconciled.
No missing study details were invented; when sample sizes or denominators were ambiguous, population labels were retained without unsupported numeric values.

Extraction emphasizes independently reviewable review-level methods, outcomes, limitations, and selected high-value study-level results; it is not a row-for-row atomization of every cell in Tables 1-3.
